children.translated_text: The <s>Prajñāpāramitāhṛdayasūtra</s> (The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom)

body.text: āryāvalokiteśvarabodhisattvo gambhīrāyāṃ prajñāpāramitāyāṃ caryāṃ caramāṇo vyavalokayati sma | pañca skandhāḥ, tāṃśca svabhāvaśūnyān paśyati sma ||
body.translated_text: <s>Āryāvalokiteśvara</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while practicing the deep <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> (perfection of wisdom), looked down and saw the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), and he saw that these are empty of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaśūnya</s>).

body.text: iha śāriputra rūpaṃ śūnyatā, śūnyataiva rūpam | rūpānna pṛthak śūnyatā, śūnyatāyā na pṛthag rūpam | yadrūpaṃ sā śūnyatā, yā śūnyatā tadrūpam ||
body.translated_text: Here, O <s>Śāriputra</s>: form (<s>rūpa</s>) is emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>); emptiness itself is form. Emptiness is not separate from form; form is not separate from emptiness. Whatever is form, that is emptiness; whatever is emptiness, that is form.
Just so [are] sensation (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), mental formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), and consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).

body.text: ihaṃ śāriputra sarvadharmāḥ śūnyatālakṣaṇā anutpannā aniruddhā amalā na vimalā nonā na paripūrṇāḥ | tasmācchāriputra śūnyatāyāṃ na rūpam, na vedanā, na saṃjñā, na saṃskārāḥ, na vijñānāni | na cakṣuḥśrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanāṃsi, na rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyadharmāḥ | na cakṣurdhāturyāvanna manodhātuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Here, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, all <s>dharmas</s> are characterized by emptiness: unproduced, unceased, unstained, not unstained, not deficient, not complete. Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, in emptiness there is no form, no sensation, no perception, no mental formations, no consciousness; no eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, or mind (<s>manas</s>); no visible form, sound, smell, taste, tangible object, or mental object; no eye-element (<s>cakṣurdhātu</s>), up to and including no mind-element (<s>manodhātu</s>).

body.text: na vidyā nāvidyā na vidyākṣayo nāvidyākṣayo yāvanna jarāmaraṇaṃ na jarāmaraṇakṣayo na duḥkhasamudayanirodhamārgā na jñānaṃ na prāptitvam ||
body.translated_text: No knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), no ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), no exhaustion of knowledge, no exhaustion of ignorance — up to and including no old age and death, no exhaustion of old age and death; no suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), no origination (<s>samudaya</s>), no cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), no path (<s>mārga</s>); no cognition (<s>jñāna</s>) and no attainment.

body.text: bodhisattvasya(śca?) prajñāpāramitāmāśritya viharati cittāvaraṇaḥ | cittāvaraṇanāstitvādatrasto viparyāsātikrānto niṣṭhanirvāṇaḥ | tryadhvavyavasthitāḥ sarvabuddhāḥ prajñāpāramitāmāśritya anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbuddhāḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, relying on the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, dwells with a veiled mind (<s>cittāvaraṇa</s>); and because of the non-existence of the veil over the mind, he is without fear, he has transcended error, and he has reached final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. All the Buddhas established in the three periods of time, relying on the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>, have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).

body.text: tasmājjñātavyaḥ prajñāpāramitāmahāmantro mahāvidyāmantro 'nuttaramantro 'samasamamantraḥ sarvaduḥkhapraśamanaḥ satyamamithyatvāt prajñāpāramitāyāmukto mantraḥ | tadyathā - gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā ||
body.translated_text: Therefore one should know the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> as the great <s>mantra</s>, the mantra of great knowledge (<s>mahāvidyāmantra</s>), the unsurpassed mantra (<s>anuttaramantra</s>), the incomparably equal mantra (<s>asamasamamantra</s>), the allayer of all suffering (<s>sarvaduḥkhapraśamana</s>); being true and not false, it is the mantra spoken in the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s>. It is thus: <s>gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā</s>.
